_note: Demo Mode - simulated/precomputed output for the bundled synthetic scenarios. No LLM call is made. 'initial' is deliberately imperfect in some scenarios so the reflection stage has something real to catch.

initial.hypothesis: Checkout requests are failing because payment-service cannot obtain database connections: the connection pool is saturated (active=20, idle=0, many waiting) and requests time out after 30s. This was most likely triggered by the deployment just before 10:30.
supporting_evidence: Pool stats show total=20, active=20, idle=0 with dozens of requests waiting
SQLTransientConnectionException: Connection is not available, request timed out after 30000ms

remediation.action: Restart payment-service pods one at a time to release held connections, then pause the long-running reporting job
remediation.expected_impact: Checkout should recover within minutes if held connections are released
remediation.risks: In-flight checkouts on a restarting pod may fail; the problem returns if the reporting job keeps holding connections
remediation.preconditions: Confirm pool saturation in metrics; at least 2 replicas so restarts are rolling
remediation.rollback: Not applicable to a restart; if errors increase, stop and escalate to the database on-call

revised.hypothesis: Checkout requests are failing because payment-service cannot obtain database connections: the connection pool is saturated (active=20, idle=0, many waiting) and requests time out after 30s. The pool filled up while very slow settlement-report queries were running, which suggests the reporting job is holding connections. No deployment evidence was found.
supporting_evidence: Pool stats move from idle=8 to idle=0 with waiting requests growing
Repeated 'Connection is not available, request timed out after 30000ms'
Slow queries of 9-26 seconds from job=settlement-report-export start before the errors
Heap and CPU look normal, which argues against memory/CPU causes
alternatives: Database server itself is slow (no DB-side metrics available)
missing_evidence: Database server metrics (CPU, locks, active sessions)
Whether the reporting job runs on the same connection pool

remediation.action: Pause the settlement-report export job and perform a rolling restart of payment-service to release held connections
remediation.expected_impact: Free connections become available; checkout latency should return to normal
remediation.risks: In-flight checkouts on a restarting pod may fail; restart alone will not prevent recurrence
remediation.preconditions: Confirm the job can be paused safely; at least 2 replicas for a rolling restart
remediation.rollback: Resume the job after the incident; a restart cannot be undone but is low risk with rolling replicas

initial.hypothesis: Order creation is slow and failing because calls to shipping-quote-service time out after 5s and are retried up to 3 times, so one order can wait 15s. The retries keep worker threads busy (50/50 active, 212 queued), which slows down all orders. The upstream carrier-rates API is responding slowly.
supporting_evidence: Repeated 'request to http://shipping-quote-svc:8080/v2/quote timed out after 5000ms'
Retry attempts 2/3 and 3/3 followed by 'retries exhausted' and 504 responses
alternatives: Order-service database slowness (but DB connections look healthy)
missing_evidence: Metrics from shipping-quote-service and the carrier API

remediation.action: Reduce shipping-quote retries from 3 to 1, lower the timeout to 2s and enable a circuit breaker with a cached fallback quote
remediation.expected_impact: Orders stop waiting 15s; worker threads are freed
remediation.risks: Some orders may use a less accurate cached quote
remediation.preconditions: Product owner agrees a fallback quote is acceptable; change made via Git
remediation.rollback: Revert the configuration commit in the GitOps repository

initial.hypothesis: inventory-service runs out of memory: the product cache keeps growing, heap usage climbs above 90%, long Full GC pauses appear, then OutOfMemoryError and OOMKilled (exit code 137) restart the pod. The cycle repeats after each restart.
supporting_evidence: product-cache size grows steadily before each crash
JVM heap used rises from ~60% to 99% of 512Mi
java.lang.OutOfMemoryError: Java heap space in ProductCache.put
container terminated reason=OOMKilled exit code 137; Back-off restarting
alternatives: Memory limit simply too small for normal load
missing_evidence: Heap dump or cache size configuration

remediation.action: Temporarily raise the inventory-service memory limit from 512Mi to 1Gi and cap the product cache size
remediation.expected_impact: Pods stop being OOMKilled while the cache fix is prepared
remediation.risks: Higher node memory use; without a cache cap the problem only takes longer to appear
remediation.preconditions: Node has spare memory; change made in Git and synced by ArgoCD
remediation.rollback: Revert the resource-limit commit in Git

initial.hypothesis: The 2.3.0 rollout of notification-service cannot start because its configuration is missing: the pod references ConfigMap 'notification-config-v2', which does not exist, and the application cannot resolve SMTP_HOST. The old 2.2.4 pods are still serving.
supporting_evidence: Application run failed: missing required property mail.smtp.host
alternatives: The ConfigMap was renamed rather than deleted
missing_evidence: Whether 'notification-config-v2' exists in the GitOps repository but was not synced

remediation.action: Fix the ConfigMap reference (create notification-config-v2 or point the Deployment back to notification-config) in the GitOps repository, then sync
remediation.expected_impact: New pods start and the rollout completes
remediation.risks: A wrong SMTP value would break email delivery
remediation.preconditions: Confirm the correct SMTP settings with the owning team
remediation.rollback: git revert the deployment change so ArgoCD restores version 2.2.4
